title: Invertibility of the specified reverse open mate
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite field extension E of Q_l. For any cartesian commutative square a; j = j'; g of schemes with j and j' open immersions, the actual natural transformation integralRingedOpenMate from a^* j'_! to j_! g^* is an isomorphism. Its component is constructed as the open-adjunction inverse transpose of a^* of the actual open unit followed by ringedSquare.inv. This is an ordinary completed-ring assertion with no quotient completion or tensor input.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence; expanded strict-system realization argument, as recorded in lem-sf-integral-canonical-ambient-models.

proof.text: The open object in X.ProEt is subterminal: cancel the open immersion to show any two maps into it coincide. Its slice-extension adjunction has invertible unit by the proved subterminal local calculus. The open-slice presentation transports full faithfulness to the actual ordinary completed-ring open extension, so its actual adjunction unit is invertible.

For an ordinary module M, pullback of its extension is in the essential image of the other ordinary open extension by the ordinary-support lemma. Full faithfulness then makes the actual ordinary counit at that pullback invertible. Apply the unit and this counit degreewise to cochain complexes. The localization_unit_app and localization_counit_app formulas express their derived versions as composites of those localized isomorphisms and the standard functor-factorization isomorphisms. Essential surjectivity of Q and naturality extend the conclusions to all unbounded derived objects.

For each M the morphism being inverse-transposed in integralRingedOpenMate is invertible: it is pullback of the invertible open unit followed by ringedSquare.inv. The adjunction inverse transpose is open extension of that morphism followed by the counit at g*(j! M). Both factors are invertible by the preceding steps. Thus each component of the specified mate is invertible, and so is the natural transformation. This uses the specified square only as an isomorphism, without a further normalization calculation.

theorem integralRingedOpenMate_isIso {U' U X' X : Scheme.{u}}
    (a : U' ⟶ U) (j' : U' ⟶ X') (j : U ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsOpenImmersion j'] (h : a ≫ j = j' ≫ g)
    (_sq : IsPullback a j' j g) :
    IsIso (integralRingedOpenMate l E a j' j g h)
